newsitem.title: USA: Domenici sees willingness to give in budget talks.
newsitem.headline: Domenici sees willingness to give in budget talks.

text.p: Senate Budget Committee Chairman Pete Domenici on Friday said both sides in the budget negotiations between Congress and the White House had indicated a willingness to give ground on some issues.

"What distinguishes this series of meetings and discussions and presentations from past efforts is that, without agreeing on things, it's pretty obvious that the administration is willing to give in some areas that are important to us, and we have indicated a willingness on our part to give in some areas that are important to them," the New Mexico Republican said.
"Has that bridged the gap of differences? Of course not -- there are still plenty," Domenici said.
The talks will continue next week.
White House Budget Director Franklin Raines said the administration was determined to keep working toward reaching a budget agreement.
"The jury's out, but we remain cautiously optimistic that if we keep at it that we can achieve the goal that the president has fully articulated and get a bipartisan budget agreeement," Raines said.
House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich, an Ohio Republican, said it was a difficult task trying to bridge the gap between two sides with such different viewpoints.

"The administration and Republican Congress have two different views of what's best for America. The question is, can we reach an agreement that compromises our positions without violating our principles?" Kasich said.
"I don't know if that can be done, because their vision of how the country ought to work and our vision of how the country ought to work is just -- we're almost worlds apart," he said.

"So when we sit down and try to bring the worlds closer together, if bringing them together means either side has to violate their fundamental principles, we won't get an agreement," Kasich said. "And that is really the test of a successful negotiation. It may be that we're just simply too far apart. We just don't know yet."
